title: After a UNEP MARS alert, operators repair a failed ball valve that released 175 t of methane in one week at the Aerial oil and gas field, Alberta, a week after detection (April 2026)
summary: Trade press relaying UNEP's August 2026 snapshot: a 175 t/week methane plume at Alberta's Aerial field in April 2026 was traced to a failed ball valve on pigging equipment and repaired within a week.
account: The Chemical Engineer reported on 4 September 2026 on UNEP's monthly snapshot of the biggest satellite-detected methane plumes recorded in August. UNEP confirmed that operators had plugged a source at the Aerial oil and gas field in southeastern Alberta, Canada. The source had released 175 t of methane (4,900 tCO2e) in a single week in April 2026. The cause was a failed ball valve connected to pigging equipment. Operators completed the repair one week after the plume was first detected. The repair followed an alert issued under UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS). The article states that UNEP does not name suspected or known operators. It states that since 2023 MARS has sent over 3,500 alerts but confirmed just 43 mitigation cases. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments. It couples that with scientific expertise and advanced AI models to notify governments and companies. The August 2026 UNEP snapshot itself is not among the sources; UNEP's snapshot page now carries the September 2026 update, which does not mention Canada. UNEP's press pages were not available and are not among the sources. The case rests on one trade-press report relaying UNEP.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators mitigate them. This case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); unnamed operators at the Aerial oil and gas field (repair)
location: Aerial oil and gas field, southeastern Alberta, Canada
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas production; intergovernmental observatory

ratings.reason: The operator found and fixed a failed valve releasing 175 t of methane a week, within one week of detection. The operator is unnamed, and no cost or further detail is reported.
A single confirmed case among about 43 since 2023, against more than 3,500 alerts. A one-week 4,900 tCO2e release was stopped.

ai_role.statement: The report credits the repair to a MARS alert and UNEP's confirmation. Only UNEP's general page describes MARS detection and analysis as using satellites with advanced AI models. The AI contribution to this specific alert is not isolated. One news item relaying the system operator's snapshot documents the event, and the snapshot itself is not among the sources.
